solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American's talking nonsense when wine is imbibed by jerk

indicators.note: something imbibed is drunk in, so the word for wine goes inside the word for jerk

parts.note: a jig is a jerky up-and-down movement
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: An American babbling while a lout knocks back his wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American's' marks the definition as a US usage: to jive is American slang for talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang, jive is glib or misleading talk, so jiving means spouting nonsense.

clue.text: A job destroyed renegade

parts.note: a post is a job or position
ate, as in 'ate away at', means destroyed

explanation.surface: A traitor who wrecked a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' looks like an anagram signal for 'A job', but it supplies ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or faith, which is what an apostate does with religion.

clue.text: Our friend is a help with login changing

indicators.note: the letters of these words change their order to form a new word

explanation.surface: A pal who helps when your login changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our friend' is written from the British viewpoint of the newspaper: someone who loves England and the English.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer of England is a friend of the English, seen from a British paper's perspective.

clue.text: After bike, communist seizes mounted horse, maybe

indicators.note: the second part follows the first, so the bike word comes before the rest

parts.note: a quad is a four-wheeled motorbike

indicators.note: to seize is to grab hold, so the communist word wraps round the other

parts.note: a red is a communist
mounted means up, as on horseback

explanation.surface: After a motorbike ride, a communist grabs a horse and rides off.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse is an example of a four-legged animal, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Fix flow backing up

indicators.note: in a down clue backing up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tide is a flow of water

explanation.surface: Repair the flow that is backing up, like a blocked drain.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix text is to correct it, which is editing.

clue.text: Fake tears upset Zoe at first

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order
at first means only the opening letter of the name is used

explanation.surface: Zoe sheds crocodile tears when upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an artificial substitute, a synonym of fake.

clue.text: Design a Morse character after US president

indicators.note: the Morse phrase follows the president's name

parts.note: James K. Polk was the 11th US president
a dot is one of the two symbols of Morse code

explanation.surface: A Morse code symbol coming after a US president's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Polka dot is a pattern of evenly spaced spots on fabric.

clue.text: Picture getting skittle for a strike

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the skittle word replaces the letter a

parts.note: an image is a picture
a pin is a skittle in bowling

explanation.surface: A photo of a skittle getting a strike in bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a strike' reads as bowling talk; 'for a' swaps PIN in for the A of IMAGE, leaving 'strike' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To impinge is to collide with or hit something, so strike is a synonym.

clue.text: Corrodes anode, a right mess finally

indicators.note: finally means each word gives only its final letter

explanation.surface: Rust eats an anode, leaving a real mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid that corrodes metal is said to eat it away.

clue.text: Experience less energy

parts.note: under means less than
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Feeling less energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through or experience it.

clue.text: Latin used badly is cut off

indicators.note: badly means the letters are set out wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Using Latin badly leaves you isolated.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulated means isolated or shielded, as in cut off from the outside.

clue.text: Follow course recording

definitions.meaning: to follow someone's trail, as a hunter does
a single song on an album

explanation.surface: Follow the course of the recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Track is a verb for trailing, a noun for a path, and a song on a record.

clue.text: Understand part of contrary bishop's argument

indicators.note: contrary means turned the opposite way, so the section is read backwards
part of means the letters are a section within these words

explanation.surface: Following some of a contrarian bishop's argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to understand it.

clue.text: Cycling fun: a character coming last is not bothered

indicators.note: cycling moves the front letter round to the back

parts.note: zed is the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A cyclist out for fun, unbothered about finishing last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' turns FUN into UNF by moving the F to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfazed means unperturbed, not put out or bothered.

clue.text: A right lavish binge runs away with church

parts.note: free, as in free with money, means lavish

indicators.note: away means the runs letter goes missing

parts.note: a spree is a binge
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone goes on an extravagant bender, then dashes off with the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs away' removes R from SPREE, leaving SPEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Free speech is a civil liberty, a right to express opinions.

clue.text: Support company leaders in panel

parts.note: to back is to support
a board of directors leads a company

explanation.surface: Backing company directors who sit on a panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A backboard is a flat board placed behind something, like a basketball hoop's panel.

clue.text: Pa perhaps in revolutionary claim, with men let out to protect base

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the anagram wraps round the base letter
out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A dad caught up in a revolutionary's claim, with men released to guard a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CLAIM MEN LET into MICALELMENT, and 'to protect' places E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pa is the symbol for protactinium, an example of a substance on the periodic table.

clue.text: Lucid old woman's taken in by coin

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the coin word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a cent is a coin
her means belonging to a woman

explanation.surface: A clear-headed old woman cheated out of a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid speech is clear and logical, which is coherent.

clue.text: River development New England excluded in critical description

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: excluded means these letters are left out

parts.note: genesis is the origin or development of something

explanation.surface: A critic's account of how a river developed, with New England left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is critical explanation or interpretation, especially of scripture.

clue.text: Most wanted by bureau, possibly, gets to work anywhere

parts.note: hot describes whatever is most in demand
a bureau is a kind of writing desk

explanation.surface: A wanted criminal working from any office desk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-desking means using whatever desk is free in an office rather than a fixed workstation.

clue.text: Defeated personnel in urban setting

indicators.note: in means placed inside the town word

parts.note: a town is an urban setting
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: HR staff beaten in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler who is thrown is beaten, so defeated fits.

clue.text: Avenger almost left, showing staying power

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: John Steed was the agent in the 1960s British TV series The Avengers

explanation.surface: An avenging hero nearly walks off, showing endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Avengers here is the British spy show, not the Marvel superheroes.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is grit or resolve, the strength to keep going.

clue.text: Amateurs spread pieces

parts.note: to lay is to spread out
men are chess or draughts pieces

explanation.surface: Amateurs spread the pieces on a game board.
explanation.definitionFit: Laymen are non-professionals, as amateurs are.

clue.text: Employer bottled by Scouse ruffian

indicators.note: bottled means kept inside, so the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: A boss attacked with a bottle by a Liverpool thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses or employs something is its user.

clue.text: Repeated an error, no men involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no means without, so the men letters are taken out

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Making the same mistake again, without any men involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OR from AN ERROR leaves ANERR, which 'involved' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Reran is the past tense of rerun, meaning repeated or broadcast again.

clue.text: Require enmity, lacking the French

indicators.note: lacking means missing these letters

parts.note: needle is ill feeling or rivalry
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Calling for hostility without the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require it.

clue.text: In a crude way, old British activity disheartened lady

parts.note: a scene is an area of activity, as in the music scene

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart of the word is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: An old British pastime upset a lady with its vulgarity.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscenely means lewdly or offensively, in a crude way.

clue.text: We yearn for variation a week after Christmas

indicators.note: variation means a changed form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: We long for a change a week after Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: January the first falls one week after December the twenty-fifth.

clue.text: Refuse to bring in Republican over Democrat's lie?

indicators.note: bringing in means introducing the party letter in place of another
over means instead of, so one party letter replaces the other

parts.note: to decline is to refuse
D abbreviates Democrat

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the Republican refuses to admit the Democrat's lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' looks like a falsehood but means lie back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lie back or rest at an angle.
